description: Wall sit with a Kegel squeeze: how to do it, where to feel it, how to breathe, common mistakes, and easier and harder versions for every level.
intro: The wall sit is a static hold with your back on a wall and knees bent. It builds endurance in the thighs and glutes, which support the pelvis. A gentle Kegel during the hold teaches the pelvic floor to work while your legs are busy, as it has to in daily life.
feel: Your thighs work steadily, with some help from the glutes. The Kegel feels like a light lift and squeeze inside, as if stopping the flow of urine, then a full release. You should not feel knee pain, breath holding, clenched buttocks doing the job or pushing down. Self-check: you can count out loud while you hold.

mistakes.right: Ninety degrees is the target, but higher is fine while you build up.

mistakes.wrong: Holding the Kegel for the whole wall sit
mistakes.right: Squeeze for a few seconds, then let go completely before the next one. The release matters as much as the squeeze.

mistakes.wrong: Holding your breath to get through
mistakes.right: Breathe steadily the whole time. If you can't, shorten the hold.

easier: Slide down only partway, hold 10–15 seconds, or leave out the Kegel until the hold feels easy.
harder: Hold toward 40 seconds and do a few short Kegels during the hold, relaxing fully between them. You can also hold a weight on your lap.
who: Good for adults over 40 who want leg and pelvic support without impact, lifters warming up, and anyone who finds moving squats hard on the knees.
skip: Modify or skip it if you have knee pain, a hernia, recent pelvic or abdominal surgery, or high blood pressure your doctor has not cleared for exercise. If your pelvic floor is tight or painful, leave out the Kegel and just breathe. Stop if it hurts.

faq.q: Should I do Kegels during a wall sit?
faq.a: Yes, gently. Squeeze and lift for a few seconds, release fully and keep breathing. If your pelvic floor tends to be tight, skip the squeeze and just hold.

faq.q: How long should a beginner hold a wall sit?
faq.a: Start with 15–20 seconds and work toward 40. Stop before your thighs shake hard.
